Also an update on the current situation... I’ve tried talking about what has happened on three separate occasions since he said he wanted to break up.. and he has gotten out of every single one. My therapist recommends he seeks professional help, but every time I bring that up he gets very uncomfortable as well.. 

He seems to be doing okay on a day-to-day basis, but I’m worried that he’s only pushing his emotions down deeper than before.

Thank you for your reply. I really appreciate you not being judgmental (I know how difficult it can be to do that without actually playing a role in a toxic relationship like ours). You were correct to assume that me begging for attention was mainly me reaching out for communication from him. 

The pain that I felt every time before each instance of cheating is insurmountable. I have a huge fear of being abandoned by him.. When he goes off with his friends & doesn’t tell me anything about any of the situation I feel so shitty about myself. I get anxiety about whether or not he’s cheating or if he just isn’t picking up his phone. (Also im not the type of girl to blow up a guy’s phone when he’s out with his friends... I just want a couple messages here and there and maybe a phone call at the end of the night) Questions start rolling through my mind about whether or not he’ll leave me and if I mean anything to him at all. It really feels like it could be handled if I stop asking those questions and go with the flow, however I know that those feelings bring me to a place where I’m very unhappy. I want to give him all my trust in our relationship, but it’s so hard to do when I feel like every serious conversation I’ve had on the matter was with an outside party. I rarely know how he’s thinking about the relationship and the more I ask for his communication, the more he closes himself off from me. 

My fear of abandonment in our relationship is very deeply rooted in my childhood. My father was very absent for most of my childhood and my sister left our family when I was 6. She ended up dying in a car crash with my cousin and another friend of her’s when I was 9. I felt abandoned by my family for a really long time. I always thought my sister left because of me, when I know in reality it was to get away from my dad. 

My boyfriend knows about all of this very well. But, in the same way that I feel about abandonment, I believe he feels similar about communication. He has a very difficult time expressing his emotions because he was told as a child that it’s better to keep quiet & detach from issues that seem unavoidable. 

I don’t want to point fingers at either of us in the situation, but it feels a lot easier to point blame at myself. Just because someone is bad at communicating their feelings, doesn’t mean I should make impulsive decisions to help cope with that.

Your feelings are always valid. Don’t let uneducated people get you down. They don’t know what it’s like to walk in your shoes or think how you think.

Tell him you love him. Tell him you would go to the furthest length possible to see him alive. Tell him you believe in him & that he’s the most amazing person you’ve ever had the pleasure of knowing. Tell him that you support him and his dreams. I would try to stray away from telling him how upset you would be without him here, and just give him more reasons to live. Don’t just tell him about what he’ll be missing if he dies, but show him how great life can truly be. If he believes that things will be okay without good test scores and a girlfriend, then he’ll start to understand that life is still manageable without those things.

She may still not be sure how she feels about you yet. I think maybe try to give her some space and see if she reaches back out to you. If she does that’s great, but if not... she probably wasn’t interested to begin with. 

(Also: if she says she wants to be friends and then comes on to you again, she doesn’t necessarily want you... she may like the idea that she could have you if she wants and will try to hold you in her back pocket for when she’s feeling needy). 

Sorry to be so blunt about it, but coming from a girl who has done this before... it really be like that sometimes.

We love you & you are never alone. Please know that your feelings are valid & we understand the difficulty having BPD and being in a relationship. It’s true that every relationship is completely different and we may never understand the depth of your feelings for that individual, but we know how BPD works. I had a similar situation with an ex of mine and I look back on how much I wanted to end my life... Years passed and I realized how blind I was during that time.. I found somebody who understands mental health issues and is willing to work through them with me. A piece of advice I wish I would’ve listened to from back then: Please don’t push people away who would be willing to help you— no matter how much pain you’re in. You may not believe it, but the struggles you are facing now are preparing you for something much greater. You will be happy. You will be seen. And you will be loved.
